stories.headline: Trump imposes tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and components under Section 232

key_facts.fact: Trump signed a proclamation on Aug. 13, 2026 imposing a 100% ad valorem tariff on drones with a maximum takeoff weight above 25 kg or with thermal imaging capabilities, plus their docking stations and certain critical components.
key_facts.excerpt: The Proclamation imposes a 100% ad valorem tariff on drones of a certain size or with certain capabilities that are particularly sensitive for national security purposes, docking stations of these drones, and certain critical components of these drones. This drone category includes drones with a maximum takeoff weight of more than 25 kilograms and drones with thermal imaging capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Smaller drones face a 25% tariff, while drones and components from the EU, Japan, Liechtenstein, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan face 15% and UK-made drones 10%.
key_facts.excerpt: A 15% tariff will be imposed on drones and components from the European Union, Japan, Liechtenstein, South Korea, Switzerland, and Taiwan, and a 10% ad valorem tariff will be imposed on drones from the UK, the White House added.

key_facts.fact: The tariffs take effect 21 days after signing; duties on components deemed not particularly sensitive take effect after 180 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The tariffs will take effect 21 days after signing. For components of drones that are not particularly sensitive, the tariffs will take effect 180 days after signing.

key_facts.fact: The proclamation cites a Commerce Department finding by Secretary Howard Lutnick that import penetration by foreign drone makers is 'substantial' and that the US is 'too reliant' on foreign drones and parts.
key_facts.excerpt: The Secretary found that import penetration from foreign producers of UAS is substantial and that the United States is too reliant on foreign sources of UAS and UAS components.

key_facts.fact: The measure relies on Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 rather than emergency powers, after the Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump exceeded his authority with earlier global levies.
key_facts.excerpt: The drone duties rely instead on Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, which requires an investigation before allowing import restrictions for national security grounds.

key_facts.fact: China dominates the market: Shenzhen-based DJI accounted for about 70% of the US commercial drone market last year, and shares of US makers AeroVironment, Aevex and Unusual Machines jumped in post-market trading.
key_facts.excerpt: China is the world's dominant manufacturer of remote-controlled aerial vehicles, with Shenzhen-based DJI Technologies accounting for about 70% of the US commercial drone market as of last year... Shares of US drone makers AeroVironment Inc. and Aevex Corp., and drone-parts company Unusual Machines Inc. jumped in post-market trading after the announcement.

stories.headline: US retail sales fall 0.6% in July, the biggest drop since May 2025 and first decline in nine months

key_facts.fact: Advance estimates put US retail and food services sales at $763.6 billion in July 2026, down 0.6% from June but up 5.0% from July 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Advance estimates of U.S. retail and food services sales for July 2026 ... were $763.6 billion, down 0.6 percent (±0.4 percent) from the previous month, but up 5.0 percent (±0.5 percent) from July 2025.

key_facts.fact: The decline, released Friday Aug. 14 by the Commerce Department, was the biggest since May 2025 and followed a revised 0.2% gain in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Retail sales fell 0.6% last month, marking the biggest decrease since May 2025, compared with a revised gain of 0.2% in June, according to the Commerce Department data released Friday.

key_facts.fact: It was the first monthly decline since October 2025, driven by nonstore retailers (-2.2%), motor vehicle and parts dealers (-1.8%), gasoline stations (-0.9%) and electronics and appliance stores (-0.5%).
key_facts.excerpt: It was the first decline since October 2025 and the biggest since May last year, driven by weaker sales at nonstore retailers (-2.2%) ... Also, sales fell at motor vehicle & parts dealers (-1.8%), gasoline stations (-0.9%) and electronics & appliance stores (-0.5%).

key_facts.fact: The control group used to calculate GDP fell 0.4%, the steepest drop since the start of 2025; excluding autos and gasoline, sales fell 0.2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Sales excluding food services, auto dealers, building materials stores and gasoline stations, which are used to calculate GDP, were down 0.4%, the most since the start of 2025.

key_facts.fact: The reading lands two days after July CPI showed inflation easing to 3.4% year-over-year from 3.5% in June, and with PPI flat on the month, weakening the case for a September Fed rate hike.
key_facts.excerpt: The July CPI and PPI figures released this week both pointed to cooling inflation, with the July PPI remaining unchanged month-on-month, below market expectations of a 0.2% increase. With retail sales now also coming in well below expectations, the Fed's policy trade-off between inflation and economic growth is shifting further toward addressing the risks of slowing demand and employment.

key_facts.fact: Part of the drop reflects Amazon moving Prime Day into late June, pulling online spending forward, while gas station receipts fell as fuel prices stayed low until Strait of Hormuz tensions resurfaced late in the month.
key_facts.excerpt: Business at gas stations fell 0.9% last month... Online sales fell 2.2% from June when they were fueled by Amazon's four-day Prime Day event that began in late June, earlier than previous years.

stories.headline: FDA clears Bristol Myers Squibb's Zenbexus, the first CELMoD approved for multiple myeloma

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 13, 2026 the FDA granted accelerated approval to ZENBEXUS (iberdomide) with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj plus dexamethasone for adults with multiple myeloma who have had at least one prior line of therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: Bristol Myers Squibb (NYSE: BMY) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved ZENBEXUS (iberdomide) in combination with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone (ZDd) for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent.

key_facts.fact: It is the first FDA-approved CELMoD, a new class of cereblon-modulating protein degraders.
key_facts.excerpt: ZENBEXUS is the first FDA-approved CELMoD, belonging to a new class called cereblon-modulating protein degraders for the treatment of multiple myeloma.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 EXCALIBER-RRMM trial the regimen doubled minimal residual disease-negative complete response rates versus the daratumumab/bortezomib/dexamethasone comparator: 41% (n=85) vs 21% (n=44), p<0.0001, at 16 months median follow-up.
key_facts.excerpt: results showed treatment with ZDd demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in one of the dual primary endpoints of minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete response (CR) in 41% of patients (n=85; 95% CI: 34-48) vs. 21% of patients (n=44; 95% CI: 15-27) treated with DVd (p < 0.0001).

key_facts.fact: It is the first approval in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma based on MRD-negative complete response; the trial randomized 939 patients and continues to assess progression-free survival, with full data expected this year.
key_facts.excerpt: This FDA decision marks the first approval in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma based on MRD-negative CR... A total of 939 patients were randomized. ... Full data from EXCALIBER-RRMM are expected this year.

key_facts.fact: The label carries boxed warnings for embryo-fetal toxicity and venous and arterial thromboembolism, and the review ran under the FDA's Project Orbis, which allows concurrent review by regulators in other countries.
key_facts.excerpt: including Boxed WARNINGS for ZENBEXUS regarding embryo-fetal toxicity and venous and arterial thromboembolism... This review was conducted under the FDA's Project Orbis initiative, which enables concurrent review by the health authorities in several other countries.

stories.headline: California clears Charter's $21.9B Cox takeover, the last hurdle to the largest US cable merger

key_facts.fact: The California Public Utilities Commission voted unanimously on Thursday, Aug. 13, to approve Charter Communications' $21.9 billion acquisition of Cox Communications, the final regulatory barrier before closing.
key_facts.excerpt: The California Public Utilities Commission voted unanimously Thursday to approve Charter Communications' $21.9 billion acquisition of Cox Communications, clearing the final regulatory hurdle before the deal closes.

key_facts.fact: Counting assumed debt the transaction is valued at $34.5 billion; California was the last of 45 states to sign off, and the FCC approved it in February.
key_facts.excerpt: California regulators voted Thursday to approve Charter's $34.5 billion acquisition of Cox Communications, the final barrier to the cable merger closing.

key_facts.fact: Conditions include five years of affordable broadband plans for low-income customers, honoring existing price-lock contracts, $30 million for a state broadband adoption fund, at least $275 million in California network upgrades and $5 million for community development financial institutions.
key_facts.excerpt: Charter committed to providing affordable broadband plans to low-income customers for five years and to keeping price-lock promises already in place... The company must also invest $30 million in a state fund covering broadband adoption, digital literacy, and device access for underserved communities, and commit at least $275 million to upgrade its California network. An additional $5 million will go to Community Development Financial Institutions.

key_facts.fact: Charter and Cox expect to close later this month, after which the combined company will operate under the Cox Communications name within a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Charter and Cox expect the transaction to close later this month, at which point the combined company will operate under the Cox Communications name within a year.

key_facts.fact: Charter is closing the deal from a position of weakness in broadband: it lost 172,000 internet subscribers in Q2 2026, taking its total to 29.4 million as fixed wireless and fiber rivals took share.
key_facts.excerpt: The company lost 172,000 internet subscribers in the second quarter of 2026, bringing its total to 29.4 million, as competition from fixed wireless and fiber providers continued to erode its home-internet business.

key_facts.fact: The merger, first announced in May 2025, creates the nation's largest internet and cable television provider.
key_facts.excerpt: California regulators voted to approve Charter Communications' $34.5 billion acquisition of Cox Communications. This vote was the final step needed before the deal becomes official. Federal officials approved the merger back in February. It was first announced in May 2025.

stories.headline: France's Constitutional Council strikes down Macron's under-15 social media ban

key_facts.fact: France's Constitutional Council ruled on Friday, Aug. 14, that Article 1 of the law banning social media for under-15s is an infringement that is 'neither appropriate, necessary, nor proportionate' to freedom of expression and communication.
key_facts.excerpt: The Constitutional Council found that Article 1 of the law championed by President Emmanuel Macron 'constitutes an infringement that is neither appropriate, necessary, nor proportionate' to the freedom of expression and communication of those under 15.

key_facts.fact: The law was due to take effect Sept. 1 and would have barred younger users from TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram, making France the first EU country with such an age limit.
key_facts.excerpt: The law, which was due to take effect on Sept. 1, would have barred younger users from social networks such as TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram, among other restrictions.

key_facts.fact: The Council also flagged privacy risks, noting the ban would force every user, including adults, to prove their age before accessing the platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: "By prohibiting minors under the age of fifteen from accessing certain online services, the law inherently requires every person, even an adult, to prove their age before accessing them," it said in its decision.

key_facts.fact: After the ruling the Elysée said Macron tasked Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu with producing a new 'legally robust' draft that accounts for the decision and the EU regulatory framework, targeting adoption by spring 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: He instructed the prime minister to draft a new, "legally sound" version of the law that would comply with the Constitutional Council's ruling and European standards. The goal is to have the revised law adopted by spring 2027.

key_facts.fact: The Council did not rule on a separate provision banning mobile phone use in high schools from Sept. 1; phones are already barred in French elementary and middle schools.
key_facts.excerpt: The Constitutional Council did not rule on a separate provision banning mobile phone use in high schools starting Sept. 1. Students are already prohibited from having phones in French elementary and middle schools.

key_facts.fact: French lawmakers had voted overwhelmingly for the bill last month, and Macron had pledged in July to enforce it by September.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, French lawmakers voted overwhelmingly in favor of this bill, which would have made it the first country in the European Union to introduce such an age limit.

stories.headline: Tether says KPMG completed its first full audit of the $180B USDT issuer, down to counting gold bars

key_facts.fact: Tether said on Thursday, Aug. 13, that KPMG U.S. audited Tether International's financial statements for the year ended Dec. 31, 2025 and issued an unqualified opinion, its first full financial audit.
key_facts.excerpt: KPMG U.S., one of the 'Big Four' accounting firms, audited Tether International's financial statements for the year ended Dec. 31, 2025 and issued an unqualified opinion, Tether said.

key_facts.fact: The audited statements showed reserves exceeding liabilities by $6.814 billion at the end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Tether said the audited statements showed reserves exceeding liabilities by $6.814 billion.

key_facts.fact: Unlike the quarterly reserve attestations Tether has published for years, the audit tested transactions, systems, valuations, counterparties and ownership records — and auditors physically counted and inspected each of Tether's gold bars.
key_facts.excerpt: KPMG examined Tether's transactions, systems, valuations, counterparties and ownership records, according to the company. Auditors also physically counted and inspected its gold bars.

key_facts.fact: USDT has grown past $180 billion in market capitalization — about $183 billion, or roughly 61% of the $301 billion stablecoin market, more than double Circle's USDC.
key_facts.excerpt: Based on DefiLlama, USDT has a market capitalisation of about $183 billion, accounting for about 61 percent of the overall stablecoin market of $301 billion. That is more than double rival Circle's USDC at about $72 billion.

key_facts.fact: Tether generated more than $10 billion in net profit in 2025 and $1.5 billion in net operating profit in Q2 2026, largely from US Treasury holdings and repurchase agreements.
key_facts.excerpt: Tether launched its USDt (USDT) stablecoin in 2014 and has since grown into one of the crypto industry's largest companies, generating more than $10 billion in net profit in 2025. In the second quarter of this year, the company reported $1.5 billion in net operating profit.

key_facts.fact: The audit answers years of doubts that followed enforcement actions: an $18.5 million New York Attorney General settlement in 2021 and a $41 million CFTC fine over claims USDT was fully backed; the full signed audit report was not published with the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2021, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered Tether to pay a $41 million penalty over statements concerning USDT's backing... Tether's announcement describes KPMG's opinion and the scope of its work, but the complete signed audit report and audited financial statements are not attached.

stories.headline: Kyiv floats a Black Sea truce as grain exports collapse; Lavrov rules out any front-line ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Ukraine sent Russia, through a third party, a proposal for a mutual halt to attacks on civilian targets in the Black Sea and was still awaiting a response on Aug. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Kyiv transmitted the proposal to Moscow through a third party and was awaiting a Russian response on August 13, according to a person familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 14 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov rejected any freeze along the line of contact, saying a halt is 'out of the question' and that Russia will intensify strikes on what fuels Ukraine's war machine.
key_facts.excerpt: "For Russia, a halt along the line of contact is unacceptable—it would negate the heroic deeds of our grandfathers and great-grandfathers who defeated Nazism. This is out of the question," Lavrov says.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian grain exports have fallen roughly 76% year-on-year so far in August as Russian attacks on ports and ships deter vessels from calling at Odesa-region terminals.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian grain exports have fallen approximately 76% year on year so far in August as Russian attacks on ports and ships deter commercial vessels from calling at Odesa-region terminals.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's drone and missile attack on Novorossiysk hit Russian warships and grain terminals; Zelenskyy said the Admiral Essen and Admiral Makarov frigates, a large landing ship and a corvette were struck, and Moscow warned of disruption to global food supplies.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy, who did not mention grain terminals, said Russia's Admiral Essen and Admiral Makarov frigates, a large landing ship, a corvette, and other vessels were struck in the attack.

key_facts.fact: Russia struck Ukraine's Danube port of Izmail on Aug. 13, damaging infrastructure and cutting power in parts of the city; Romania scrambled two fighter jets after an aerial target briefly entered its airspace.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia attacked Izmail again on August 13, damaging port infrastructure, triggering a fire and causing power outages in parts of the city. Romania scrambled two fighter jets after an aerial target briefly entered Romanian airspace during the attack.

key_facts.fact: Moscow said on Aug. 13 it was ready to resume peace talks and saw no obstacle to meeting US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, after Kyiv handed Washington new proposals on Aug. 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Karasin assured that the Kremlin sees no obstacles to holding a meeting with the US President's special envoy Steve Witkoff and the American leader's son-in-law Jared Kushner.
